name: Primary Cutaneous Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma Not Otherwise Specified

criteria.description: Presence of atypical peripheral T-cell infiltrate in the skin with epidermotropism and/or dermal involvement
T-cell lineage confirmed by immunohistochemistry with aberrant loss of pan-T-cell markers and expression of cytotoxic markers
Exclusion of other defined cutaneous T-cell lymphoma subtypes and systemic T-cell lymphomas
Presentation with solitary or multiple skin lesions without evidence of extracutaneous disease at diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of peripheral T-cell lymphoma in skin biopsy with immunophenotypic confirmation and exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent solitary or multiple erythematous to violaceous plaques or nodules
searchTerms: persistent red or purple skin patches
skin ulcers related to cancer spots

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Indurated skin plaques with variable scaling
Constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever and night sweats

occasional.symptomName: Erythema and edema surrounding skin lesions
searchTerms: redness and swelling around skin spots
skin redness with puffiness near lesions
weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (high fever, drenching night sweats, significant weight loss)

searchTerms: severe skin tissue death with ulcers

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing atypical T-cell infiltrate with epidermotropism
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD4 or CD8 with loss of pan-T-cell markers
imaging: PET-CT scan to exclude extracutaneous involvement
CT scan of chest, abdomen, and pelvis for staging
genetic: Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR
No specific recurrent chromosomal translocations identified
other: Flow cytometry of skin or blood may show aberrant T-cell populations
Exclusion of systemic T-cell lymphoma by bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Usually solitary nodules with spontaneous regression

redFlags: Evidence of extracutaneous spread on imaging
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Bekkenk MW, Geelen FA, van Voorst Vader PC, et al. Primary and secondary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphomas: a clinicopathologic study of 73 cases. Arch Dermatol. 2000;136(3):309-319.
